_design_note: The learning-rate schedule arm. Its only difference from F2 is learning_rate_schedule L00 -> L01: 5e-4 decaying linearly to 1e-4 over 2500 rounds, then held. The motivation is not that the step size level matters -- section 7.24 established that, and a level mattering does not make a schedule useful. It is the shape of F2's own curve: from round 2250 to 5000 its score oscillates between 13.1 and 13.9 and coins_share between 0.240 and 0.271 with no trend (section 7.26.2). That is what a step size too large for the remaining gradient looks like. If that reading is right the oscillation shrinks; if F2 has genuinely converged, nothing changes and the reading is wrong.

_predeclared_design_numbers.changed_factor: learning_rate_schedule L00 -> L01 (route R02_8 -> R02_9); the two routes differ in that field alone
_predeclared_design_numbers.falsification: Spread over rounds 2500-5000 within noise of F2's means the oscillation is not a step-size artefact; drop the schedule and record it as a negative result.
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction: None stated on the mean. The predicted effect is on the spread.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reporting: Report the checkpoint-to-checkpoint spread, all five training-seed distributions, coins_share and the death split.
_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_loot_crate: Two arms measured once each need a gap of 4.7 on loot-crate.
_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_tournament: Section 7.26.3: a single tournament measurement settles nothing. Repeat the classic_versus_opponents suite ten times, as F2 and M3.13 were.
_predeclared_design_numbers.the_metric_that_decides_it: NOT the mean. Compare the standard deviation of the primary-suite score across the checkpoints from round 2500 to 5000 against F2's. A lower mean with a lower spread still falsifies the reading; a similar mean with a similar spread means F2 was converged.
